new_findings.title: consecutive_progressing_cycles=4 counts windows not boredom clock cycles — semantics may mislead
new_findings.description: The consecutive_progressing_cycles field value (4) equals the number of windows in cells_over_time. The code increments this counter for each window with new_shapes_introduced > 0, working from newest to oldest. Since all 4 windows introduced at least 1 new shape, the counter is 4. However, each window is 1 hour, and the naming implies 'cycles' which to a reader might suggest boredom timer cycles (~30 min each). The value 4 in a 4-hour lookback is not a signal of exceptional progress — it is the maximum possible value given the window count.
new_findings.evidence: code: 'for (let i = 0; i < cells_over_time.length; i++) { if (cells_over_time[i].new_shapes_introduced > 0) consecutive_progressing_cycles++; else break; }' — counter = window count when all windows have introductions. Live value: 4 = numWindows = 4.
new_findings.action: Cosmetic/doc issue. Field is internally consistent. Consider renaming to consecutive_windows_with_new_shapes or adding a numWindows field to make the ceiling explicit.
